site.name: pulsegrid
site.summary: PulseGrid Fictional bulk-power-system SCADA / EMS dashboard "PulseGrid" for the Western Interconnect. UXBench fixture in the Dashboard category. Pages - `index.html` — **Overview**. Left rail nav (6 entries with alarm badge); top bar with BA selector (Western / ERCOT / SPP / MISO), Production / Replay / Plan tabs, live ticking clock, ⌘K, theme toggle, alert bell, operator avatar; 5 KPI cards (demand / generation / frequency / renewables share / active alarms) each with sparkline; **2-column body grid**: 48-hour load chart with actual / forecast (dashed) / net renewables area + "NOW" marker, weather card with 4 zones (Phoenix 112°F driving 1.8 GW cooling load, Tehachapi wind, etc.), 24-cell generator status grid (color-coded online / tripped / ramping / maintenance with output + % capacity), active-alarms list with severity dots (critical pulses), live fuel-mix bars (7 fuels), interchange table with 6 tie-lines (sched / actual / Δ). - `generators.html` — **Generator list** (38 units across the fleet). Filter strip with status pills (All / Online / Ramping / Tripped / Maintenance), fuel and zone selectors, and search. Sortable-style table with EMS ID, plant name, fuel-color icon, zon

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full pulsegrid system, prioritizing the primary dashboard flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The PulseGrid dashboard presents a visually dense but functionally compromised experience, particularly in critical workflows like alarm management and mobile operations. While the visual hierarchy effectively highlights KPIs, core interactive controls suffer from broken state logic (filters failing to update lists) and poor mobile ergonomics (sub-44px tap targets). Accessibility gaps, such as unlabeled form inputs, further degrade usability for assistive technology users.

exploration_plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of PulseGrid, a fictional SCADA/EMS dashboard, focusing on information hierarchy, critical alert handling, and data visualization clarity across desktop and mobile viewports.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will begin with the Overview dashboard to assess high-level situational awareness (KPIs, charts). It will then drill down into specific workflows: managing active alarms, filtering the generator fleet, and analyzing load forecasts. The run will conclude by validating global controls (BA switching, theme toggle) and checking mobile responsiveness for critical tap targets identified in the prescan.
assumptions: The 'Topology' and 'Events' pages are likely stubs or placeholders as indicated by '#' hrefs in the prescan; exploration will prioritize functional pages.
The application relies heavily on visual status indicators (colors/icons) which must be validated for accessibility and clarity.
The 'Replay' and 'Plan' modes in the top bar may alter data views significantly and require validation.
risk_hotspots: Alarm Acknowledgement Flow (alarms.html): Critical for safety systems; needs clear feedback.
Generator Status Filtering (generators.html): Complex filtering logic (status + fuel + zone) prone to UI clutter.
Mobile Navigation: Prescan indicates multiple small tap targets (<44px) in the sidebar and top bar.
Chart Interactivity: Hover states and tooltips on the load chart (index.html) and forecast chart (forecast.html).

phases.title: Overview Dashboard & Global Controls
phases.objective: Validate the primary situational awareness view and global navigation elements.
key_checks: Verify KPI cards display clear trends (sparklines) and status colors.
Test 'Western Interconnect' BA selector dropdown for options (ERCOT, SPP, MISO).
Toggle 'Production', 'Replay', and 'Plan' tabs to observe data context changes.
Hover over 'System load' chart to verify tooltip data availability.
exit_criteria: Global nav items respond to interaction.
Theme toggle visually updates the interface.

phases.title: Alarm Management Workflow
phases.objective: Assess the usability of the alarm list for rapid identification and resolution.
key_checks: Review default sort order and severity highlighting (Critical vs. Major).
Test filtering by Severity (Critical only) and Status (Open/Acked).
Attempt to 'Acknowledge' a single alarm and verify state change.
Test 'Acknowledge selected' bulk action if checkboxes are present.
Verify time-range filters (Last 1h, Last 24h) update the list.
exit_criteria: Filters correctly narrow the alarm list.
Severity colors are distinct and legible.

phases.title: Generator Fleet Inspection
phases.objective: Evaluate the efficiency of finding specific assets within a large dataset.
key_checks: Use search input to find a specific unit (e.g., 'Palo Verde').
Check pagination or scrolling behavior for the full list of 38 units.
Click 'Details →' on a generator to check for modal or page transition (if available).
exit_criteria: Search results are accurate and fast.
Combined filters do not break the layout.
Status pills clearly indicate current fleet health.

phases.title: Forecast Analysis & Mobile Responsiveness
phases.objective: Validate predictive data visualization and ensure critical controls are usable on mobile.
key_checks: On Forecast page: Toggle between 'Day-ahead', 'Hour-ahead', and 'Real-time' models.
On Forecast page: Check table/chart synchronization when hovering rows.
Attempt to tap small controls (Theme toggle, BA selector) to identify touch target failures.
exit_criteria: Forecast model switching updates the chart data.
Mobile menu is accessible and navigable.
Critical alerts are visible without horizontal scrolling on mobile.

findings.user_goal: Filter alarms by severity or status to isolate specific issues.
findings.problem: Filter controls on the Alarms page appear functional but fail to update the visible data list. Selecting 'Critical only' or 'Acknowledged' leaves unrelated items (e.g., Major/Minor or Open/Resolved) visible in the table.
findings.evidence: Session memory notes: 'The Severity dropdown was set to Critical only, but the alarm table still displays rows with major and minor severity badges.' Similar failure observed for Status filters. This creates a false sense of security or confusion about the system state.
findings.why_it_matters: In a SCADA/EMS context, operators rely on filters to triage emergencies. If filters do not work, operators may miss critical alerts hidden among noise or waste time investigating already-resolved issues, leading to potential operational delays.
findings.suggestion: Debug the client-side filtering logic to ensure the table view strictly reflects the selected filter criteria. Provide immediate visual feedback (e.g., row count updates) when a filter is applied.

findings.user_goal: Navigate and interact with the dashboard on a tablet or mobile device.
findings.problem: Critical navigation links and control buttons have tap targets significantly smaller than the recommended 44px minimum height, increasing the risk of mis-taps and frustration.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag elements like 'Production' tab (25px height), 'Overview' link (37px height), and filter pills (27px height) as below the 44px mobile guidance. The Generators page also exhibits horizontal overflow (505px content vs 390px viewport), forcing awkward scrolling.
findings.why_it_matters: Field operators often use mobile devices for quick checks. Small touch targets lead to accidental navigation or failed interactions, while horizontal overflow hides critical data columns (like Output/Capacity) unless explicitly scrolled.
findings.suggestion: Increase padding on navigation items and buttons to meet the 44px minimum touch target guideline. Implement responsive table strategies (e.g., card view or horizontal scroll containers) for the Generators list on mobile.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Navigation rail; generators.html: Table layout

findings.user_goal: Use screen readers or keyboard navigation to operate the interface.
findings.problem: Multiple form controls, including Severity, Status, Time filters, and the Balancing Authority selector, lack explicit labels, aria-labels, or placeholders, making them difficult to identify for assistive technologies.
findings.evidence: DOM summaries flag 'missing_input_label' for ux-10 (Severity), ux-11 (Status), ux-12 (Time), and the BA selector. These elements rely solely on visual proximity or internal text which may not be exposed correctly to screen readers.
findings.why_it_matters: Operators with disabilities or those using voice-command systems cannot efficiently use these filters, violating accessibility standards and potentially excluding qualified personnel from using the tool effectively.
findings.suggestion: Add visible labels or aria-label attributes to all select inputs and dropdowns. Ensure the Balancing Authority selector has a clear label indicating its purpose.
findings.source_hint: alarms.html: Filter dropdowns; index.html: BA Selector

findings.user_goal: Switch between Production, Replay, and Plan modes to analyze historical or future data.
findings.problem: The 'Replay' and 'Plan' mode toggles provide weak or ambiguous visual feedback. Clicking 'Replay' changes the chart time range but does not clearly highlight the button itself, leaving the user unsure if the mode is active.
findings.evidence: Observations note that clicking 'Replay' activated the '48h' chart selector but the 'Replay' button itself remained visually similar to the inactive 'Production' tab. In some instances, no visible change occurred at all.
findings.why_it_matters: Ambiguous state indicators cause cognitive load. Users may not realize they are viewing historical data, leading to decisions based on outdated information rather than live grid conditions.
findings.suggestion: Implement distinct active states (e.g., filled background, bold text, or underline) for mode tabs. Consider adding a global banner or indicator when 'Replay' or 'Plan' mode is active.

findings.user_goal: Access the Topology or Events pages for deeper system insights.
findings.problem: Navigation links for 'Topology' and 'Events' point to '#' stubs, resulting in no page change or content update upon clicking.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Topology' resulted in a hash change (index.html#) but no visual state change or content load. These appear to be non-functional placeholders in the current build.
findings.why_it_matters: Dead links break user trust and workflow continuity. If these features are planned, they should be disabled or marked 'Coming Soon' to prevent confusion.
findings.suggestion: Either implement the missing pages or disable the links with a tooltip explaining their unavailability.
